# Edward — Complete Documentation

> An open-source AI assistant that remembers, notices what matters and works on your Mac, for one person. The Claude API for every model call; macOS on Apple silicon only.

Website: https://meet-edward.com
GitHub: https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward
Operating guide for AI assistants: https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
License: Apache 2.0

---

## Introduction

*An open-source AI assistant that remembers, notices what matters and works on your Mac, for one person: you.*

### What Edward is

Edward is a personal assistant you run yourself, on a Mac that stays on. You talk to him in an app you can install on your phone, by voice, and in iMessage, where anyone can write `@Edward` in a chat. He keeps what he learns in your own PostgreSQL database, with a record of where each memory came from. He has a small computer of his own (a sandboxed shell, a file editor and a headless browser), he schedules his own follow-ups when he promises to check back, and he keeps a journal of what he did on his own and why.

Every model call goes to the Claude API, with a model chosen per purpose and a daily spend cap you set ($5 by default). The code is Apache-2.0 on [GitHub](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward).

This release is a snapshot of a build that ran every day for one person for months. The parts that were bespoke to that home are marked `ADAPT:` in the code and collected in [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting).

![Edward's Today page: late pet doses to log, a call starting soon, a reply held for approval, and a list of what he did today](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/today-desktop.png)
*Today: what needs you, with the action on each card, and what he did. (Invented data from the repository's UX harness.)*

### What makes him different

- **He remembers, and knows where he heard it.** Every memory records who said it (you, someone in your messages, or Edward himself), what it is about and how sure he is. Ask him “how do you know that?” and he answers from the record. Only your own words make a standing instruction, and only you can change what you said.
- **He works for one person.** Edward runs on your Mac and keeps everything he knows in your Postgres. The one outside service he needs is the Claude API, which sees what each model call sends it.
- **He has his own computer.** A persistent shell, a file editor and a headless browser of his own, with rails against accidents: he can’t write his own running code, read his own keys, reach your database or launch other apps. The sandbox guards those things, not your whole account (see [Guard rails](https://meet-edward.com/docs/guard-rails)).
- **He follows through.** When he says he will check back, he schedules it and comes back. Whatever he does on his own goes in a journal entry, and you can mark each one right or wrong.
- **He speaks up once, or not at all.** Noticing what matters in your messages is opt-in. When it is on, he says a thing once, through one door, outside your quiet hours.
- **He has limits you set.** A daily spend cap in dollars, a per-turn cap, a secret scan on everything that leaves, and approvals when you want them.

### How a conversation works

1. You write (or say) something in the app, in iMessage, or through the iPhone widget.
2. Edward searches his memories (vector similarity and keywords, blended 70/30) and the documents he keeps for you.
3. Claude answers with the same fourteen tools on every surface: his shell and editor, web search and fetch, his own browser, your Chrome if you allow it, `look` for pictures and PDFs, your messages, one guarded send, a way to tell you something, memory, scheduling, his screens and a visible plan. The app shows his reasoning and every tool call as it happens.
4. After the answer, a small model extracts what is worth remembering and files it with its source.

### When nobody is talking to him

- **Follow-through.** A promise to check back is a scheduled wake; when it fires, he does the checking.
- **A silent nightly** at 03:00 tidies his memory and his state, and is skipped when nothing happened.
- **Free time**: one small, budgeted run a day at 13:00 for his own screen and projects. It reaches nobody.
- **Noticing** (off until you turn it on): he reads new messages and mail for what matters to you, decides whether it is worth a word, and says it once.

More in [The mind](https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind).

### What leaves your Mac

Edward’s memories, conversations, documents and files live in your Postgres and your home folder. What goes out:

- **The Claude API** receives what each model call sends: the conversation, the memories retrieved for it and the tool results.
- Only if you set them up: ElevenLabs (voice), Google (Gmail), Twilio (SMS), Brave Search, Home Assistant, and whatever a page or a send he makes for you reaches.

### What you need

- A Mac with Apple silicon that can stay on (a Mac mini makes a good host)
- The Xcode command-line tools, [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) and an [Anthropic API key](https://console.anthropic.com/)

Intel Macs, Linux and Windows are not supported. See [Platform support](https://meet-edward.com/docs/platform-support) for why.

### Choose your path

- **[Beginner guide](https://meet-edward.com/docs/beginner-guide)** — never used a terminal? Start here.
- **[Set up with AI](https://meet-edward.com/docs/setup-with-ai)** — let Claude Code (or another coding assistant) walk you through it.
- **[Quick start](https://meet-edward.com/docs/getting-started)** — comfortable in a terminal? Four commands.
- **[Upgrading from March](https://meet-edward.com/docs/upgrading)** — already running the March 2026 release? Move to this one without losing what he knows.

The repository’s own docs go deeper: the [README](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/README.md), [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) (the operating guide) and one page per subsystem in [docs/architecture](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/README.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/introduction

---

## Beginner guide

*From a Mac to a running Edward, one step at a time. No experience needed.*

### What you will need

- **A Mac with Apple silicon** (an M1 or later) that can stay on and stay logged in. Edward runs on this Mac, so when it sleeps, he does too. A Mac mini makes a good always-on host. Intel Macs are not supported.
- **An Anthropic API key**, which is how Edward talks to Claude. You pay Anthropic for what he uses, and Edward stops himself at a daily cap ($5 by default; you can change it).
- **About 30 minutes**, most of it waiting for things to download and install.

### Step 1: Open Terminal

Terminal is the Mac app for typing commands. You don’t need to know how it works: paste exactly what this guide shows and press Return.

1. Press `Cmd + Space` to open Spotlight
2. Type **Terminal** and press Return

### Step 2: Install Apple’s command-line tools

```
xcode-select --install
```

A window asks to install the tools. Click **Install** and wait for it to finish. If Terminal says they are already installed, move on.

### Step 3: Install Homebrew

Homebrew installs the software Edward is built on (Python, PostgreSQL and Node). Paste this and press Return:

```
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

It asks for your Mac password. Nothing appears while you type it; that is normal. When it finishes, it prints **Next steps** with two or three commands that add Homebrew to your path: paste those too. Then check:

```
brew --version
```

### Step 4: Get an Anthropic API key

1. Go to [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/) and sign in or create an account
2. Add a payment method or credits under Billing
3. Open **API Keys** and click **Create Key**
4. Copy the key (it starts with `sk-ant-`). The setup script asks for it in the next steps. Treat it like a password: don’t paste it into a chat or an email.

### Step 5: Get the Edward code

```
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward.git
cd meet-edward
```

This puts Edward in a `meet-edward` folder in your home folder. Keep it there rather than on the Desktop or in Documents, which macOS guards from background programs like Edward’s services.

### Step 6: Run the setup script

```
./setup.sh
```

It asks three things:

- **Your name**, which Edward calls you by
- **Your Anthropic API key** from step 4
- **Your time zone**, which reminders, quiet hours and “today” follow

Then it installs Python 3.12, PostgreSQL 16 and Node, builds the memory search extension, creates Edward’s database, downloads his Python and web packages and his headless browser, and builds two small helpers. It takes a while, and a lot of text scrolls past. It is safe to run again if anything stops it.

At the end it prints the path of a `python3.12`. Copy it somewhere: you need it if you want Edward to read your messages or calendar (step 10).

### Step 7: Start Edward

```
bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh
```

This keeps Edward running: macOS starts him now and every time you log in, and restarts him if he stops. It also sets up a health check every five minutes and a nightly backup to `~/edward-backups`.

The first start takes a few minutes: the backend downloads its small memory model and the app builds itself. To watch it, run `tail -f /tmp/edward-backend.log` (press `Ctrl + C` to stop watching).

### Step 8: Choose your password

On the Mac that runs Edward, open your browser and go to `http://localhost:3000`. The first visit asks for a password and a **one-time setup code**. Get the code in Terminal:

```
cat backend/.setup_code
```

Type it in (capitals and dashes don’t matter) and choose your password. The code is deleted once the password is set. It exists so nobody else on your network can claim your Edward first, which is also why the first password can only be set on this Mac.

### Step 9: Turn on what he may use

On a fresh install Edward can use none of his skills until you turn them on. Open the **Edward** tab, then:

1. **Mind → Skills**: turn on what you want him to have. Shell/Bash is his own computer (a shell and a file editor), Web Search lets him search and read pages, iMessage lets him read and send messages, Push Notifications lets him reach your phone, and iOS Widget lets him fill the iPhone widget.
2. **House → Locale**: check the time zone.

Then go to **Chat** and say hello. If he answers, Edward is running.

### Step 10 (optional): Let him read your Mac’s apps

Edward reads Messages, Mail, Calendar, Reminders and Contacts from their own databases, which macOS protects. Grant access only for what you will use:

- **Full Disk Access**: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access → **+**, press `Cmd + Shift + G`, paste the python path from step 6, and turn it on.
- **Calendars and Reminders** (so he can add and change events when you ask): sitting at the Mac, run `bash backend/scripts/eventkit_request_access.sh` and click Allow.
- **Automation**: macOS asks the first time Edward sends a message. Answer it at the Mac.

Reading your messages is still off until you turn on **Attention → Listening → Configuration → Messages** in the Edward tab. Read [Listening & pings](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening) first: with it on, anyone can write `@Edward` in a chat with you and he answers from your own iMessage account.

### Keeping the Mac awake

Edward runs as your user, so the Mac must be on and you must be logged in. In System Settings → Energy, turn on “Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off” (on a laptop, keep it plugged in). After a restart, log in and Edward starts by himself.

### Using Edward from your phone

Installing the app on your phone, push notifications and the microphone all need an `https://` address. The usual way is a tunnel to port 3000 on your Mac:

- [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/) keeps Edward private to your own devices.
- [Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/) gives him a public address. To try it: `brew install cloudflared`, then `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000`, which prints a temporary `https://…trycloudflare.com` address. For a lasting one, set up a named tunnel and run it as a LaunchAgent.

Then tell Edward where he lives: add `EDWARD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-address` to the `.env` file in the `meet-edward` folder (links in his pushes use it), and the tunnel’s LaunchAgent label as `EDWARD_TUNNEL_LABEL` so the health check watches it. Run `./restart.sh` to apply.

Open the address on your phone and sign in. On iPhone, tap Share → **Add to Home Screen**; on Android, the ⋮ menu → **Add to Home screen**.

### Common problems

#### “brew: command not found”

The Homebrew installer’s “Next steps” weren’t run. Close Terminal, open a new window and try again; if it still fails, run the commands Homebrew printed at the end of step 3.

#### Setup stops with an Intel or Rosetta message

Edward needs Apple silicon. If your Mac is Apple silicon, your Terminal is running under Rosetta: quit it, then in Finder → Applications → Utilities, select Terminal, press `Cmd + I` and untick “Open using Rosetta”.

#### The page says “still starting”, or won’t load

The first start can take several minutes. Watch `tail -f /tmp/edward-backend.log` and `tail -f /tmp/edward-frontend.log`, then try again. `./restart.sh` restarts both.

#### I signed in but keep landing back on the login page

You are probably on a plain `http://` address other than `localhost`. Use the Mac itself, or an `https://` tunnel (above). On a home network you trust, `EDWARD_COOKIE_SECURE=off` in `.env` also works.

#### He says he can’t read my messages or calendar

Full Disk Access is missing, or went to a different python. The path changes when Homebrew upgrades Python, so grant the new one (setup and the LaunchAgent installer both print it) and run `bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh` again.

#### Is everything working?

Open `http://localhost:3000/api/health/report` while signed in: it lists what works and what doesn’t.

Next: [Configuration](https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration) lists the settings, and what ships switched off. The repository’s [README](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/README.md#quick-start) has the same steps in brief.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/beginner-guide

---

## Set up with AI

*Let an AI coding assistant walk you through the install, one step at a time.*

### Why it works

Edward’s repository carries its own operating guide, [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CLAUDE.md), written for AI assistants working in it. Its section “Helping someone set up Edward”, lists the steps in order: prerequisites, the setup script, your settings, the macOS permissions, starting him, choosing your password, and the optional features. An assistant that can run commands, such as [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), can follow it with you, explain each step and fix what goes wrong.

### What you need

- **A Mac with Apple silicon** that can stay on
- **An AI coding assistant** that can run terminal commands on that Mac: Claude Code, or a similar tool
- **An Anthropic API key** from [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/) (your assistant can show you where to make one)

### Paste this to your assistant

Open your assistant in a terminal on the Mac that will run Edward (for Claude Code, run `claude` in your home folder) and paste:

```
I want to set up Edward, an open-source personal AI assistant, on this Mac.

1. Check that this Mac has Apple silicon, the Xcode command-line tools and Homebrew.
2. Clone https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward.git into my home folder.
3. Read the CLAUDE.md at the top of that checkout and follow its section
   "Helping someone set up Edward", one step at a time. Explain each step
   and confirm it with me before the next.

Never ask me to paste my Anthropic API key, a password or the setup code
into this chat: I will type them into ./setup.sh or .env myself.
```

If you already cloned the repository, open the assistant inside the `meet-edward` folder instead: Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md` by itself there, so “Help me set up Edward” is enough.

### What to expect

1. It checks the prerequisites and installs what is missing (it will ask before it does).
2. It runs `./setup.sh`, which asks *you* for your name, your API key and your time zone. Type them into the setup script, not into the chat.
3. It helps you grant only the macOS permissions you need, and starts Edward, usually with `bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh` so he stays on.
4. You open `http://localhost:3000` on the Mac and choose a password. The first visit also asks for a one-time setup code: read it yourself with `cat backend/.setup_code`.
5. It checks the time zone and what works, using the app’s health report and the logs, then walks you through the optional features you want.

> **Keep your secrets out of the chat.** What you paste into an AI assistant is sent to its provider. Your API key belongs in `./setup.sh` or `.env`, and your password and setup code in Edward’s own sign-in page.

### After setup

In the Edward tab, turn on the skills you want under **Mind → Skills** (every skill starts off), and check **House → Locale**. To reach Edward from your phone, see [Using Edward from your phone](https://meet-edward.com/docs/beginner-guide#using-edward-from-your-phone).

The same assistant is a good partner for fitting Edward to your own home later: [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting) has prompts written for it.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/setup-with-ai

---

## Quick start

*For the terminal-comfortable: install, start, choose a password.*

### You need

- A Mac with Apple silicon that can stay on (a Mac mini makes a good host)
- The Xcode command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`) and [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
- An [Anthropic API key](https://console.anthropic.com/)

### 1. Install

```
git clone https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward.git && cd meet-edward
./setup.sh          # installs everything, asks for your name, API key and time zone
```

`./setup.sh` is safe to run again; each step checks what is already there. It stops before installing anything on an Intel Mac or in a Rosetta shell. It installs `python@3.12`, `postgresql@16` and `node` with Homebrew, builds pgvector from source for Postgres 16, creates the `edward` database, makes `backend/.venv` with pinned dependencies, installs Playwright’s headless shell, runs `npm ci`, builds two small Swift helpers (media and EventKit), and writes `.env` from `.env.example`.

| Flag | What it adds |
| --- | --- |
| `--with-test-db` | the backend tests’ own Postgres cluster on :5433 |
| `--launchagents` | runs `scripts/install-launchagents.sh` at the end |
| `--no-helpers` | skips building the Swift helpers |
| `--non-interactive` | never prompts; takes `EDWARD_OWNER_NAME`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `TIMEZONE` from the environment |

### 2. Start Edward, one of two ways

**Always on** (the usual choice for the Mac that hosts him). launchd starts him now and at every login, and restarts him if he stops:

```
bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh
```

It installs the backend (:8000), the frontend (:3000), a health check every five minutes plus a deeper one at 08:00, a nightly backup at 03:30 (to `~/edward-backups` unless `EDWARD_BACKUP_DIR` says otherwise) and a daily memory report, labelled `com.meet-edward.*`. It takes `--with-graph`, `--without-backup`, `--dry-run` and `--uninstall`. If you started Edward by hand from this checkout, it stops that copy first.

**By hand.** He runs until you stop him or the Mac restarts:

```
./restart.sh        # backend :8000, frontend :3000
```

With the agents loaded, `./restart.sh` (or `./restart.sh backend|frontend`) restarts through launchd. It only restarts its own checkout’s Edward: in a second clone it refuses (exit 78) to touch agents that run another one.

The first start takes a few minutes: the backend downloads its embedding model and sets up the database, and the frontend runs its first production build. `./restart.sh` waits up to 2 minutes for the backend and 4 for the frontend, then says “still starting” and exits 0. Logs: `/tmp/edward-backend.log` and `/tmp/edward-frontend.log`.

### 3. Choose a password, on the Mac itself

Open `http://localhost:3000` on the Mac that runs Edward. The first visit asks for a password and a one-time setup code:

```
cat backend/.setup_code
```

The backend writes the code when it starts with no password set; only your macOS user can read it, and it is deleted once the password is set. Until then the API answers nothing but the sign-in pages, and the setup request must come from a page at `localhost` on this Mac. No screen on the Mac? Forward the port and read the code over ssh:

```
ssh -L 3000:localhost:3000 you@my-mac.local
ssh you@my-mac.local cat <your checkout>/backend/.setup_code
```

### 4. After you sign in

1. **Edward tab → Mind → Skills.** Every skill starts off on a fresh install. Turn on what Edward may use: Shell/Bash (his computer: `bash` and the editor), Web Search, iMessage, Push Notifications, iOS Widget.
2. **House → Locale.** Check your time zone: reminders, quiet hours and “today” follow it.
3. **macOS permissions** (System Settings → Privacy & Security), only for what you use:
  - **Full Disk Access** for the python `setup.sh` prints at the end: iMessage, Mail, Contacts, Calendar and Reminders are read from their databases through it. Started by hand with `./restart.sh`, macOS charges your terminal app instead, so grant that too.
  - **Automation**: macOS asks the first time Edward sends a message or drives Chrome.
  - **Calendars and Reminders** (for changes): run `bash backend/scripts/eventkit_request_access.sh` while sitting at the Mac.

### Reaching him from your phone

Installing the PWA, push notifications and the microphone all need HTTPS. Put a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, ngrok) or a reverse proxy in front of port 3000, set `EDWARD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to that address, and name the tunnel’s LaunchAgent in `EDWARD_TUNNEL_LABEL` so the health check watches it. The backend listens on every interface so devices on your network (a hub) can reach it; `EDWARD_BACKEND_HOST=127.0.0.1` keeps it to this Mac. Behind a tunnel, leave uvicorn’s `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` unset: sign-in limits read the client from the tunnel’s own headers.

### Is it working?

- `GET /api/health/report` (signed in) says what works: turns and tool failures, pings, the calendar, mail, the last memory report, spend, and whether the app’s time zone matches the Mac’s.
- `GET /api/health/spend` shows today’s Claude spend against the cap.
- The watchdog writes to `~/.edward-health/health.log`.

### Common issues

#### Signing in loops back to the login page

The session cookie is `Secure`, which assumes HTTPS (browsers make an exception for `http://localhost`). Use HTTPS, or set `EDWARD_COOKIE_SECURE=off` on a plain-HTTP network you trust.

#### Messages, Mail or Calendar can’t be read

Full Disk Access is tied to the python binary’s path, so `brew upgrade python@3.12` silently breaks it: grant the new path and re-run `bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh` and `bash backend/scripts/eventkit_request_access.sh`.

#### pgvector is missing after a Postgres reinstall

`brew reinstall postgresql@16` removes the pgvector built from source. Run `./setup.sh` again.

Next: [Configuration](https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration) (every setting, and what ships off), or [Upgrading from March](https://meet-edward.com/docs/upgrading) if you ran the March 2026 release. The [README](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/README.md) is the canonical version of this page.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/getting-started

---

## Configuration

*Who you are, where he runs, what he may spend, and what ships switched off.*

### Where settings live

Everything is in `.env` at the top of your checkout. `./setup.sh` creates it from [`.env.example`](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/.env.example), which describes every setting with its default. The backend loads the file itself (a variable already set in its environment wins), and the start scripts never export it. Most values are read on every call; to be sure a change applies, run `./restart.sh backend`. Never commit `.env`.

### The essentials

`./setup.sh` asks for these three:

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `EDWARD_OWNER_NAME` | What Edward calls you. Unset, he says “the owner”. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Your key from [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/). Every model call uses it. |
| `TIMEZONE` | Your IANA zone (`America/New_York`), until the app’s own setting (Edward tab → House → Locale) is loaded. |

### About you

Read by `backend/services/owner.py`. The code never names its owner any other way.

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `EDWARD_OWNER_FULL_NAME`, `EDWARD_OWNER_ALIASES` | Other names you go by, so he recognises you in messages. |
| `EDWARD_OWNER_HANDLES` | Your phone numbers, emails and Apple ID: how he recognises your iMessages and your self-chat. Set it if he reads your messages. |
| `EDWARD_OWNER_EMAILS` | Your email addresses: mail from these is yours, and he never emails you. |
| `EDWARD_HOUSEHOLD` | The people at the household hub, comma-separated, you first. |
| `EDWARD_SENSITIVE_NAMES` | Pets, family and anyone else whose mentions his memory upkeep must never retire on its own. |

### This Mac

Read by `backend/services/host_config.py`.

| Variable | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EDWARD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` | Where you open Edward (a tunnel’s https address). Links in pushes and texts use it. |
| `EDWARD_TUNNEL_LABEL` | unset | Your tunnel’s LaunchAgent label, so the health check watches and restarts it. |
| `EDWARD_BACKEND_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | The backend listens on every interface so a hub on your network can reach it; `127.0.0.1` keeps it to this Mac. |
| `EDWARD_COOKIE_SECURE` | `on` | The session cookie assumes HTTPS (or `http://localhost`). `off` only on a plain-HTTP network you trust. |
| `EDWARD_LAUNCHD_PREFIX` | `com.meet-edward` | The LaunchAgents’ label prefix. |
| `EDWARD_BACKUP_DIR` | `~/edward-backups` | Where the nightly backup goes. A `/Volumes/…` path is a removable drive (skipped while unplugged; needs Full Disk Access). |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | the base URL | The app’s public origin for link previews, baked into the frontend build: after changing it, run `bash frontend/deploy-build.sh` and restart the frontend. |

### The model and the money

`EDWARD_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` is the default: every call goes to the Claude API, with one route per purpose.

| Route | Used for | Model, effort |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat` | your conversations, ping replies, scheduled events | Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| `mind` | every wake: follow-through, the nightly, free time, speaking up | Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| `pulse` | deciding what the widget and screens show | Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| `background` | memory extraction and upkeep, the noticer, photo descriptions | Haiku 5.5, high |
| `voice` | spoken turns | Sonnet 5.5, low |
| `judge` | evaluations | Opus 5.5, high |

Override any of them per purpose with `EDWARD_CLAUDE_<PURPOSE>_MODEL`, `_EFFORT`, `_MAX_TOKENS`, `_THINKING_DISPLAY` and `_CACHE_TTL` (for example `EDWARD_CLAUDE_CHAT_MODEL`).

| Variable | Default | What it bounds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EDWARD_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` | `5` | Dollars over your local day. Background work stops at 60 % of it (`EDWARD_BACKGROUND_SPEND_SHARE`), Edward’s own turns at the cap, and your own turns may run `EDWARD_INTERACTIVE_RESERVE_USD` (3) past it. |
| `EDWARD_TURN_MAX_USD` | `3.00` | One turn you asked for. |
| `EDWARD_AUTONOMOUS_TURN_MAX_USD` | `1.00` | One turn you didn’t (a wake, a ping from a friend, an event). |
| `EDWARD_CREDITS_START_USD`, `EDWARD_CREDITS_START_DATE` | unset | Set both to count prepaid credits down on the Fuel card (console.anthropic.com stays the authority). |

Every call is priced and shown in the app (Edward tab → Work → Usage) and at `GET /api/health/spend`.

**The Codex fallback**: `EDWARD_LLM_PROVIDER=codex` runs GPT through the Codex CLI’s ChatGPT login. That is not an official API for third-party apps, may break at any time and may conflict with OpenAI’s terms; use it at your own risk. `OPENAI_API_KEY` switches it to the public API.

### Off by default, and the switch for each

A fresh install reads nothing private and reaches no one. Each feature below stays off, or does nothing, until you turn it on.

| What | How to turn it on |
| --- | --- |
| Every skill | Edward tab → Mind → Skills (Shell/Bash, Web Search, iMessage, Push Notifications, iOS Widget, Voice…) |
| Reading your iMessages, and `@Edward` pings | Edward tab → Attention → Listening → Configuration → Messages; Full Disk Access; Messages on this Mac signed into your Apple ID; `EDWARD_OWNER_HANDLES`. Pings then follow `EDWARD_PINGS` (on). [Read this first](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening). |
| Mail.app | Listening → Configuration → Email; Full Disk Access; keep Mail.app running |
| Gmail | An OAuth client (`GMAIL_CLIENT_ID`, `GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET`; [gmail-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/gmail-setup.md)), then Attention → Gmail → Watch my inbox |
| Noticing (speaking up unasked) | `EDWARD_PROACTIVITY=shadow` (decides, never speaks), then `notice` |
| Hands in your Chrome | Load `chrome-extension/` unpacked in Chrome, then `EDWARD_CHROME_HANDS=on` |
| His shell, editor, your Chrome and the screens in friends’ pings | `EDWARD_FRIENDS_FULL_TOOLSET=on`, at a risk: a friend’s message then drives a shell that runs as you |
| Approvals for tainted turns | `EDWARD_TAINT_APPROVALS=shadow` (log only) or `on` |
| Voice | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` |
| Push notifications | `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys` into `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` / `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, then allow notifications in the app (HTTPS) |
| The hub’s pets and care | Copy `backend/hub_seed.example.json` to `backend/hub_seed.json`, describe your own, set `EDWARD_HUB_SEED=hub_seed.json` |
| The hub’s people | `EDWARD_HOUSEHOLD` (just you until set) |
| The household photo door (a photos-only login) | `PHOTO_DOOR_PASSWORD_HASH`: a bcrypt hash, in single quotes (`.env.example` has the command) |
| Twilio SMS and WhatsApp (a number of Edward’s own) | `TWILIO_*` and `EDWARD_OWNER_HANDLES`. Webhooks are refused without `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, and only your own numbers get an answer; `EDWARD_TWILIO_ANSWER_ANYONE=on` answers everyone, at a risk |
| The WhatsApp bridge | Run the `whatsapp-mcp` Go bridge yourself, then `MCP_WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true` |
| apple-mcp (a fallback for reading your calendar) | Install bun, clone apple-mcp, `MCP_APPLE_ENABLED=true` |
| Alexa and Home Assistant | `ALEXA_SKILL_ID`, `HOME_ASSISTANT_URL`, `HOME_ASSISTANT_TOKEN`. Inbound Alexa requests are not signature-checked yet: leave `ALEXA_SKILL_ID` unset unless you use the skill |
| Brave Search | `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`, only needed with the Claude server-side web tools off (`EDWARD_SERVER_WEB_TOOLS=off`) or on the Codex fallback |
| The knowledge graph | `GRAPHITI_ENABLED=true` (queues every new memory) **and** `GRAPHITI_INGEST_ENABLED=true` (fills the graph from the queue), then `bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh --with-graph`. Each memory costs a few background model calls |
| Hosted pages | `HTML_HOSTING_URL` and `HTML_HOSTING_API_KEY`. There is no default host |
| A daily cap on his own pushes | `EDWARD_PUSH_BUDGET=<n>` (none by default) |
| Deep health checks for a hub kiosk and for mail | `EDWARD_HEALTH_HUB_KIOSK=1`, `EDWARD_HEALTH_EMAIL=1` |
| The Codex fallback | `EDWARD_LLM_PROVIDER=codex` (unofficial, at your own risk) |

### On by default

Know these before you leave Edward running:

- **The daily spend cap**, $5 over your local day.
- **Quiet hours**, 22:00–07:00 (`EDWARD_QUIET_HOURS=22-7`; equal hours mean none). Pushes and spoken lines wait for morning.
- **Two scheduled wakes a day**: a silent nightly at 03:00, skipped when nothing happened, and one free-time run at 13:00 (about $0.50 at most) that reaches nobody.
- **The surfaces pulse**: a check every 15 minutes that runs a model turn only when the board, the calendar, a screen or the widget changed.
- **The nightly backup** at 03:30 to `~/edward-backups`, on the same disk, unless you install with `--without-backup` or point `EDWARD_BACKUP_DIR` elsewhere. Keep a copy off the Mac too.
- **The late-dose alert** (`EDWARD_CARE_WATCH=on`), which has nothing to watch until the hub has timed care items.
- **The egress secret scan** and **the shell sandbox**. Their `off` values are emergency switches only.

### Everything else

The full annotated list is [`.env.example`](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/.env.example); the environment section of [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) has the main ones with their defaults on one screen. Nothing reads `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `USPS_API_USER_ID` or the LangSmith variables any more.

The iPhone widget has its own token, set up in [Widget, screen & hub](https://meet-edward.com/docs/surfaces).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration

---

## Platform support

*macOS on Apple silicon, and nothing else, for now.*

| Platform | Supported | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon | Yes | Everything works. |
| An older macOS, Apple silicon | Without calendar changes | The EventKit helper needs macOS 14, so `setup.sh` warns and Edward runs without it: he can read Calendar and Reminders but not change them. |
| Intel Macs, or a Rosetta (x86_64) shell | No | `setup.sh` stops before installing anything. |
| Linux, Windows (WSL) | No | `setup.sh` stops on anything but macOS. |
| Docker | No | The backend runs natively on macOS, never in a container. |

> The March 2026 release described Linux and WSL as mostly working. This release does not: Edward’s own computer, his listeners and his follow-through all lean on macOS now.

### Why Apple silicon

Edward’s memory search uses a small local embedding model through sentence-transformers, which pulls in PyTorch. The pinned PyTorch (in `backend/constraints.txt`) publishes no x86_64 macOS wheel, so `setup.sh` stops on an Intel Mac, in a Rosetta shell, or with an x86_64 Python. That pin, not the Swift helpers, is what an Intel port would have to change.

### Why macOS

- **His shell is sandboxed by Seatbelt** (`sandbox-exec`). Without it the `bash` tool fails closed rather than running unsandboxed.
- **He reads Apple’s own databases**: Messages’ `chat.db`, Mail’s Envelope Index, the Calendar and Reminders stores, Contacts. He sends iMessages through AppleScript and changes your calendar through EventKit.
- **launchd keeps him running**, and the macOS privacy grants (Full Disk Access, Automation, Calendars) decide what he may read.
- **His media handling uses macOS tools** (`sips`, `afconvert`, `avconvert`) and a Swift helper, not ffmpeg.

### What a port would take

A port is a project, not a setting. The macOS seams are marked `ADAPT:` in the code and collected in [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting), which has prompts for an AI assistant for the two pieces a Linux port would start with:

1. **A sandbox for the `bash` tool first** (bubblewrap or firejail), rendered from the same rails table as the macOS profile and failing closed in the same way.
2. **systemd units** in place of the LaunchAgents, with the same options as `scripts/install-launchagents.sh`.

Everything that reads an Apple app (iMessage, Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, the screen) already degrades with an honest error when it can’t, so a port could leave those off.

### Where the other pieces run

- **Your phone**: the app is a PWA, so any modern phone browser works, over HTTPS (see [Quick start](https://meet-edward.com/docs/getting-started)).
- **The household hub**: any browser in kiosk mode on `/hub`; the reference install used a Raspberry Pi with a 7″ touchscreen ([pi-hub-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/pi-hub-setup.md)).
- **The iPhone widget**: the Scriptable app.
- **Hands in your browser**: Google Chrome with the unpacked Edward extension, on the same Mac.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/platform-support

---

## Upgrading from March

*Move a March 2026 Edward onto this release without losing what he knows.*

This page is for an Edward installed from the March 2026 public release (`main` up to commit `408e1d5`, or the `v1.0.0` tag). A fresh install needs none of it: start at [Quick start](https://meet-edward.com/docs/getting-started). The full version, with every command and edge case, is [docs/UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/UPGRADING.md) in the repository.

**The short version:** stop Edward, back up the database, pull, move the old Python environment aside, run `./setup.sh`, tidy `.env`, start him. The first start migrates the database in place. Plan on half an hour, most of it installs and the first frontend build.

### What changes

Almost everything around the memory store. Your memories, documents, conversations, files, scheduled events, password and settings are kept. What Edward can do, and how, is new:

- **Every model call goes through the Claude API**, one route per purpose, under a **daily spend cap** ($5 by default). The model you picked in March is replaced by the route’s.
- **One toolset of 14 tools on every surface**, and a sandboxed computer of his own. The Python/JavaScript/SQL sandboxes, Lightpanda and self-evolution are gone.
- **The heartbeat’s triage is replaced by the mind**: wakes, follow-through, a silent nightly, a journal and (opt-in) noticing.
- **@Edward pings in iMessage are answered** by default if he reads your messages (step 8).
- **The app is new**: Today is the front door, the Edward tab replaces the old settings page, and the frontend runs as a production build.

### 1. Stop Edward

The March `restart.sh` ran the backend on :8000 and `npm run dev` on :3000:

```
lsof -t -iTCP:8000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill
lsof -t -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill
```

If you made your own launchd job or login item for him, unload it first.

### 2. Back up

```
PG="$(brew --prefix postgresql@16)/bin"
mkdir -p ~/edward-backups
"$PG/pg_dump" -Fc -d edward -f ~/edward-backups/edward-march-final.dump
"$PG/pg_restore" --list ~/edward-backups/edward-march-final.dump | head

cp .env ~/edward-backups/env-march
cp backend/.jwt_secret ~/edward-backups/jwt_secret-march 2>/dev/null
cp -R backend/storage ~/edward-backups/storage-march 2>/dev/null
```

Keep the dump until you have used the new Edward for a while; the nightly backup’s rotation never touches that name.

### 3. Pull the release

```
git pull
```

Put any changes of your own on a branch first: this release rewrites most files, so expect to port them by hand. A fresh clone works just as well (copy `.env`, `backend/.jwt_secret` and `backend/storage/` into it); the database is shared, not part of the checkout.

### 4. Move the old Python environment aside

```
mv backend/.venv backend/.venv.march
```

This release needs Homebrew’s Python 3.12 and installs pinned versions, so a clean environment is simplest.

### 5. Run setup

```
./setup.sh
```

It keeps your `.env` and asks only for what is empty: your name, the API key if missing, your time zone. It builds pgvector for Postgres 16 when it is missing (the March setup used a Homebrew bottle that no longer ships), creates the venv, installs Playwright’s headless shell, runs `npm ci` and builds the Swift helpers. It stops on an Intel Mac or under Rosetta.

At the end it prints the python that needs **Full Disk Access**. Grant it even if you granted one in March: the permission belongs to a binary’s path, and the new environment may run on a different python.

### 6. Update .env

Compare yours with [.env.example](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/.env.example). The backend reads only the `.env` at the repo root (move a `backend/.env` up), and a variable set in your shell or by launchd now wins over the file. The changes that matter:

| Setting | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2`, `LANGCHAIN_API_KEY`, `LANGCHAIN_PROJECT` | **Delete.** LangSmith support is gone, but LangChain would keep sending traces while they are set. |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Delete; nothing reads it. |
| `EDWARD_OWNER_NAME`, `EDWARD_OWNER_HANDLES`, `EDWARD_OWNER_EMAILS`, `TIMEZONE` | New. Who you are, and how he recognises your own messages. |
| `EDWARD_INSTRUCTION_HORIZON_SINCE` | New. **Set it to the day you upgrade** (e.g. `2026-10-12`), so the weekly memory upkeep leaves the instructions March stored alone instead of letting the ones it can’t trace to you lapse. |
| `TWILIO_*` | Webhooks now check Twilio’s signature and need `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`; only your own numbers get an answer (`EDWARD_TWILIO_ANSWER_ANYONE=on` brings back answering everyone, at a risk). |
| `HTML_HOSTING_URL`, `HTML_HOSTING_API_KEY` | No default host any more; set both if you used hosted pages. |
| `EDWARD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `EDWARD_COOKIE_SECURE` | New. Your tunnel’s https address, if you use one; the cookie setting only for a plain-HTTP network you trust. |
| `EDWARD_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` | New, default 5. March had no cap. |

### 7. Start him

```
bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh   # always on
# or
./restart.sh                           # by hand
```

The first start builds the frontend and migrates the database; watch `/tmp/edward-backend.log`. Sign in with your March password. The one-time setup code is only for an install with no password; if your March Edward never had one, set it on the Mac with `cat backend/.setup_code`.

### 8. Check what he listens to

- **Mind → Skills.** Your March switches carry over. Shell/Bash is now his whole computer, Web Search gates search and fetch, iMessage gates reading and sending. Code Interpreter, JavaScript and SQL say “Retired”.
- **Attention → Listening.** March turned Messages on by default. If Edward read your iMessages then, he reads them now, and he now **answers @Edward in any chat, from anyone** (friends inside limits, unknown numbers held for you), from your own iMessage account. If you don’t want that, turn Messages off in its Configuration view; `EDWARD_PINGS=off` alone is not enough.
- **House → Locale.** Check the time zone: reminders, quiet hours, the nightly and “today” follow it.
- **Work → Events.** Your reminders and recurring tasks are kept; check their times in your zone.

Two optional steps (adopting this release’s persona, and backfills that tidy March data) are in [UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/UPGRADING.md), as is **rolling back** to March.

### What is gone

| March feature | Now |
| --- | --- |
| Self-evolution (Edward proposing, testing and deploying changes to his own code) | Gone, its tables dropped. He keeps a **wishlist** for you instead (Work → Wishlist) and never promises to build what he wishes for. |
| Browser automation through Lightpanda | Gone. His own browser is Playwright’s headless shell, and with `EDWARD_CHROME_HANDS=on` he can use your Chrome. |
| Python, JavaScript and SQL sandboxes | Gone. His sandboxed shell runs python, node and sqlite3. |
| LangSmith tracing | Gone. Each turn’s reasoning, tools and memory hits are stored with the answer and shown in the chat’s work rail. |
| Morning briefing, meeting prep, open-loop nudges, pattern detection | Gone. Wakes (follow-through, the nightly) and opt-in noticing replace them. |
| The heartbeat’s triage and its calendar listener | Gone. Listening stores what arrives and hands it to the mind; the calendar is read when needed. |
| Self-service install of MCP servers | Edward can’t install servers himself any more. Servers you installed still load, and you manage them in Mind → Servers. |
| The persistent-database, file-storage and hosted-page tools | Out of his toolset (he has his own home folder). Your saved files and databases are kept and browsable in the Memory room. |

### What is dormant

**Workers and coding sessions.** The orchestrator, its routes and the Workers panel are still in the tree, and March tasks stay in their table, but no tool in the default toolset starts a worker any more: long work is a background job in his own shell plus a scheduled wake. The coding-session code now drives the Codex CLI inside a sandbox, and is equally dormant.

### What is new

- **Memory with provenance**: who said it, about whom, a tier, a source; weekly upkeep that never deletes; one question at a time about contradictions; a forget that previews exactly what it removes. [Memory](https://meet-edward.com/docs/memory)
- **His computer**: a sandboxed shell, an editor, web search and fetch, a headless browser, `look`. [His computer](https://meet-edward.com/docs/computer)
- **The mind**: wakes, follow-through, the nightly, free time, a journal with your verdicts, opt-in noticing. [The mind](https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind)
- **Pings and media in iMessage**: @Edward in any chat; photos, PDFs, voice messages and videos understood. [Listening & pings](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening)
- **The app**: Today, a work rail that shows his thinking live, live voice, the Edward tab, `/screen`, the household hub, push with quiet hours. [The app](https://meet-edward.com/docs/app)
- **Guard rails**: a secret scan on everything that leaves, spend caps, a one-time setup code, a sandbox for his shell, friends’ pings without your machine, Twilio answering only you. [Guard rails](https://meet-edward.com/docs/guard-rails)
- **Running it**: LaunchAgents, a health watchdog, nightly verified backups, staged frontend deploys with a one-command rollback.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/upgrading

---

## The app

*Three tabs, three questions: what needs me, let’s talk, and what is Edward up to.*

Edward’s app is a progressive web app served by your Mac on port 3000. Open it in any browser, or install it on your phone’s home screen (that needs an `https://` address; see [Quick start](https://meet-edward.com/docs/getting-started)). The same Edward, with the same memory and conversations, is behind every surface: the app, voice, iMessage, the widget and the screens.

### Today

The front door, and where the app opens. In order:

- **What needs you**, each with its action on the card: a message thread waiting on you, an event about to start, a send held for your approval, a note Edward left, a late pet dose. Cards never flood: one per thread, one per note title.
- **Today’s digest**, and a short line from Edward that only the real signals support.
- **What I did**: what he did since last night, grouped by part of the day. What he chose to do on his own links to its journal entry.
- **Your conversations.**

![Edward's Today page: late pet doses to log, a call starting soon, a reply held for approval, and a list of what he did today](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/today-desktop.png)
*Today: what needs you, with the action on each card, and what he did. (Invented data from the repository's UX harness.)*

A send is never a keyboard shortcut: it goes out from your number, so it is always a deliberate tap, and the card says “Sent” only when the message was delivered.

### Chat

- **The work rail.** Above each answer, one timeline of what he did to get there, live: memory searches, each reasoning step by its heading, every tool call in plain words (“Opened example.com”, “Searched memory for …”, “Texted Parker”), code and its output, plans. When the answer starts, it folds into a receipt (“Thought for 14s · searched memory · opened 2 pages”), and a tap reopens it. His thinking and tool use are always visible; that is a design rule, not a debug option.
- **Yours and Edward’s.** The sidebar keeps your conversations apart from Edward’s own threads: his journal entries (led by what he did on his own), message threads he read, scheduled events.
- **Drafts and attachments** stay with their thread; what you type while he is answering waits in a queue, and Stop halts the turn in flight.
- **Links**: `/chat?c=<id>` is a conversation, `?prompt=` fills the composer without sending, `?voice=1` opens live voice.

![A chat with Edward: his work rail lists a memory search, a document search, a page he couldn't read and a web search, above his answer with a cost table](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/chat-desktop.png)
*The work rail: every step he took, including the one that failed.*

### Voice

With `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (and `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` for the voice he speaks in) and the Voice skill on:

- **Voice memos**: the mic button records a memo, posted as a playable attachment with its transcript, or transcribed into the text box.
- **Live voice**: a hands-free (or hold-to-talk) conversation. Edward streams captions as you speak, answers out loud, says a short bridge line when he needs a moment, and stops when you talk over him. A long task hands off (“I’ll keep working on that”) and carries on in the background.
- **Mic sensitivity** has three levels; the default gates out the room’s background noise, such as a TV.

Spoken turns use the `voice` route (Sonnet 5.5 at low effort) for a fast first word. Audio goes to ElevenLabs for speech to text and back.

### The Edward tab

What he knows, watches and does. It opens on “Edward now”: him, his status and the start of his own state page, then five rooms:

| Room | What is in it |
| --- | --- |
| Mind | His thoughts and wakes, the journal, the model, skills, MCP servers |
| Memory | Memories (with where each came from), documents, files, databases, and Dreaming: how he tidies his memory, and any “Which is right?” question |
| Attention | Listening (messages and mail), notifications, proactivity, Gmail, Alexa |
| Work | Events and reminders, workers, his wishlist, usage (the day’s spend) |
| House | Locale (your time zone), the hub’s photos |

![The Edward tab: Edward's status, what he knows, watches and does, and the five rooms](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/edward-tab-desktop.png)
*The Edward tab: what he knows, watches and does, and the five rooms.*

Every status line comes from a real signal. Edward’s animation makes the same promise: he looks busy only when something is running.

### Push notifications

- Web Push to the devices where you allowed it, once you set VAPID keys and turn on the Push Notifications skill.
- Everything Edward sends on his own goes through one door: quiet hours (22:00–07:00 by default) hold it until morning, except a late pet dose or travel closing within three hours; he follows up once, never twice; and nothing secret goes on your lock screen.
- Every push is logged with where its tap leads, and the tap goes there.
- Notes that can wait land on Today instead of buzzing your phone.

### A menu-bar companion

`companion/EdwardBar` puts Edward in the menu bar of any Mac you use. It tells him you are at that Mac and whether you are active, idle or away (never what is on your screen; sharing the frontmost app’s name is off by default), and opens the chat. Build notes are in [its README](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/companion/EdwardBar/README.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/app

---

## Memory

*What he remembers, where he heard it, and who may change it.*

### The store

Every memory is a row in your PostgreSQL database with an embedding from a small local model (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, 384 dimensions, run on your Mac). Retrieval blends **70 % vector similarity** (pgvector) with **30 % BM25 keyword matching**: the first finds “dog” when you asked about pets, the second finds “Biscuit” when you named her.

A memory has a type:

| Type | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `fact` | “Biscuit is a beagle, born in 2019” |
| `preference` | “Prefers window seats” |
| `context` | “Is in Springfield until Friday” |
| `instruction` | “Don’t reply in the family chat without asking” |
| `intention` | Something Edward decided to do or watch, with a horizon |

### Provenance: where he heard it

Every row also records where it came from, so he can tell what you said from what he read or concluded:

- **Origin**: `heard` (you said it), `read` (he read it in a message, a page or a screen), `thought` (he concluded or decided it) or `did` (an action and its outcome).
- **About**: you, a contact, Edward himself, or the world.
- **Tier**: observation → belief → knowledge, climbing as it is confirmed. A dated episode (“the flight on 3 June 2026 was late”) stops at belief.
- **Source**: the conversation, turn, message or page it came from.

Ask “how do you know that?” and he answers from that record, and only from it. The Memory room shows the same record for every row.

### Only your words are yours

A memory counts as something you said only when it came from your own turn: your chat, your voice, the widget, Alexa, your self-chat, or your own words in an `@Edward` ping. A wake, a scheduled reminder, someone else’s message or the household hub’s voice can’t write a memory as yours. And only you can change or forget what you said: from a turn that isn’t yours, his memory tools refuse to touch it. An instruction you want kept for good can be pinned as confirmed, and nothing retires or rewrites a pin.

**Standing instructions** are your own instructions about yourself. They ride along in every wake, ahead of everything else.

### After each turn

- **Extraction.** A small model (the `background` route, Haiku 5.5) reads the turn and files what is worth keeping with its type, importance, tier and source. A near-duplicate reinforces the existing row instead of adding one.
- **Use is citation.** A memory counts as used only when the answer actually drew on it, not whenever it was retrieved, so popular rows can’t entrench themselves.
- **Reflection** looks for related memories in the background and hands them to the next turn.
- **Search tags** make the conversation findable later.

Before a turn, **deep retrieval** runs a few rewritten queries alongside yours when the message is short or the conversation has run on, and memories linked to the people and places you mention come along too.

### Horizons

Some things are meant to lapse. A one-off preference (“no onions in tonight’s order”) or a temporary instruction gets a 30-day horizon; an intention from a wake gets 72 hours unless a scheduled follow-up holds it. Telling him a taste is lasting takes the horizon off.

### Upkeep that never deletes

- **Weekly decay** (Sunday’s nightly) retires stale rows by stamping an end date. It never deletes, and one command undoes a pass. It never retires anything sensitive (pets, health, family, money, someone in distress, and the names in `EDWARD_SENSITIVE_NAMES`), stated timeless facts, or your own instructions.
- **Hourly consolidation** links related memories and merges true duplicates, never your own words.
- **Contradictions**: at most five new flags an hour, one per pair. If neither side is your own word, he keeps both. If one is, he asks you, one “Which is right?” at a time, on Today.

### Documents

Beside memories he keeps whole documents: recipes, notes, lists, reference pages, and his own `Edward: state` page, which he rewrites on Sundays. Documents are searched the same way, and their titles come up in conversation when relevant. Browse them in Memory → Documents.

### Forgetting

Ask him to forget something and he first shows the plan: the memories that match (whole words, linked entities, close meanings) and what hangs off them. He deletes exactly that plan, checks, and logs only the counts. Only you can ask, in your own conversation, and you can’t forget yourself (that would take the whole store). The Memory room has a “Forget…” sheet that does the same.

### The knowledge graph (optional)

Edward can also keep a graph of people, places and how they relate (Graphiti on Kuzu), filled by its own worker. It is off by default and takes two switches; see [Configuration](https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration#off-by-default). Each memory costs a few background model calls.

The long form, with the reasons behind each rule, is [memory.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/memory.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/memory

---

## The mind

*What Edward does when nobody is talking to him, and how you can tell.*

### Proactivity is noticing, not a schedule

An earlier Edward ran on a timetable: a morning briefing, meeting prep, nudges about open loops, a weekly pattern report. On the install this release comes from, almost none of it was read. What was valued were the catches: a deadline closing, two messages that disagreed, someone waiting only on its owner. So Edward now wakes for a reason, does what that reason needs, and otherwise stays quiet.

### What wakes him

| Wake | When | What it may do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Follow-through** | A follow-up he scheduled, usually because he promised to check back | The checking, then tell you. A promise made in an iMessage chat is kept in that chat. |
| **The nightly** | 03:00, skipped when nothing happened | Close finished intentions, note what he learned, update his state page; on Sundays, review the week and run memory upkeep. Silent: at most one note, never a push or a message. |
| **Free time** | 13:00, once a day | Whatever he chooses for his screen and his own projects, about $0.50 at most. It reaches nobody. |
| **Speaking up** | The noticer found something worth a word (opt-in, below) | Check it, then say it once. |
| **The surfaces pulse** | Every 15 minutes, only if something changed | Decide what the widget and the screens show. See [Widget, screen & hub](https://meet-edward.com/docs/surfaces). |

A wake is an ordinary turn with the same 14 tools as a conversation; what it may do is set by its policy. A wake that reaches nobody can’t send or push however it tries, and a refused call comes back as an honest error the model can read. The `mind` route runs Sonnet 5.5, inside the daily spend cap and a $1 cap per turn.

`@Edward` pings are not wakes: they have their own runner, which answers each one within the limits in [Listening & pings](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening).

### The thought journal

Edward needs no approval to act, but it must be obvious when he chooses to. A wake that does something outward (a message, a push, a note) or commits to something (scheduling, standing down) writes a journal entry:

- **Why I looked**
- **What I noticed**
- **What I did**, one line per action, “sent” only when it was
- **Why**

Each entry asks you: **Right call? Yes / No.** The next wake reads your verdicts. Entries lead Edward’s side of the chat sidebar, marked when he reached someone, and you can reply inside one to ask why: he answers from what he actually saw and did.

### Noticing (opt-in)

With Listening on, Edward stores what arrives in your messages and mail. Whether he reads it for what matters is `EDWARD_PROACTIVITY`:

| Value | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `off` (default) | Messages are stored, pings answered, promises kept, the nightly runs. Nothing is noticed. |
| `shadow` | The noticer and the gate run and record each decision, but he never speaks. Try this first. |
| `notice` | The whole path. |

The path:

1. **The noticer** (a small model) reads each new batch of messages, with your own lines from every chat, and writes down private noticings: a deadline, a conflict between two facts, someone waiting only on you, a travel time closing, a password you pasted somewhere. Each must cite the messages it came from.
2. **The gate**, plain code, decides: silent, hold, a note on Today, a push, or a reply in the thread. You are already on it? Silent. Just arrived? Wait 15 minutes. Said it before with nothing new? Silent. Only travel or household items closing within three hours may push, and quiet hours hold the rest until morning.
3. **The speaker**, a wake, checks the noticing against the messages and says it once, through `tell_owner`.

Your own instructions bind the gate (“don’t push me about the soccer chat”). What he learns from being ignored only shapes his advice to himself; it never silences a category.

### How he reaches you

Everything Edward says to you on his own goes through one door, `tell_owner`: quiet hours (22:00–07:00 by default) held in code, except care alerts and travel closing within three hours; at most one follow-up per subject; an offer phrased as an offer (“Want me to reply? Not sent.”); no secret on a lock screen. The channel is `EDWARD_OWNER_CHANNEL`: a push (the default), your iMessage self-chat, or Edward’s own Twilio number (with those two, an urgent word is a text). A wake never messages you any other way: `send_message` refuses to.

**The late-dose alert** is code, not a model: a timed pet medication on the hub left unlogged 45 minutes after its slot pushes once. It works with every other switch off and outside the spend cap.

### Rules a wake keeps

- A mention must be answered, unless one of your standing instructions says stay out.
- He doesn’t start or join other people’s conversations unasked: messages go out from your number, so he tells you instead.
- A wake can’t change or delete what you said, and is never given the tool that forgets.
- A failed wake is retried only when the failure was transient, and never after it reached someone or committed to something.

### Watching him think

- `GET /api/mind/now` is his live state (what is running, his last and next wake); the app’s Edward reflects it.
- Mind → Thoughts lists each wake, what it did, and your verdicts.
- `POST /api/mind/wake` wakes him by hand (it answers 202 and runs in the background).

### Before you leave him unattended

The repository has evaluation gates that run the real model over recorded situations on a test database, with every outward act a dry run: the judgement check (a mention, a standing instruction, a follow-through, the silent nightly; about $1–4), a ping check, and a noticer check to run before `EDWARD_PROACTIVITY` goes past `off`. See [testing.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/testing.md).

The long form: [mind.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/mind.md), [noticing.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/noticing.md) and [push-and-notes.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/push-and-notes.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind

---

## Listening & pings

*What he reads, who can ask him things, and what he may do for them.*

> **Edward reads and sends iMessages as you.** He uses the Apple ID that Messages on the host Mac is signed into, and his messages go out from your own account, signed as Edward. With Messages turned on, anyone can write `@Edward` in a chat with you and he answers there. Decide that you want this before you turn it on.

### Listening

Three listeners store what arrives, and do nothing else. Each is off until you turn it on in the Edward tab: Messages and Email under **Attention → Listening → Configuration**, Gmail under **Attention → Gmail → Watch my inbox**.

| Listener | How | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iMessage | Reads `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` every 10 seconds | Full Disk Access; Messages signed into your Apple ID; `EDWARD_OWNER_HANDLES` |
| Mail.app | Reads Mail’s own index for unread inbox mail | Full Disk Access; Mail.app kept running |
| Gmail | Google’s API, with “Watch my inbox” on | An OAuth client of your own ([gmail-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/gmail-setup.md)) |

What is stored feeds the mind: Edward can read it when you ask (“what did Rowan say about Saturday?”), and, if you turn noticing on, he reads each batch for what matters (see [The mind](https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind)). A message thread waiting on you shows on Today as one card per thread, and “Done” clears it.

Mail can never trigger him: anyone can type `@edward` in a subject line, so only an iMessage can ask Edward anything.

### Pings

A ping is an iMessage that asks Edward something:

- `@Edward` from anyone in any chat (yours included)
- anything you write in your own self-chat
- a reply to one of Edward’s messages

Each ping gets its own turn, with the chat’s recent lines, its people, the photos and PDFs in it, and the links in the message, and his answer goes back into that chat. Pings are recorded the moment the message is stored, and answered by their own runner, so they are never lost in a busy batch. A ping closes when his reply is confirmed delivered (read back from Messages), or when he records that he chose not to answer. If a send went out and something failed after it, he says he was cut off rather than answering twice.

Your own pings carry your authority: what you tell him in your self-chat or in your own `@Edward` is remembered as yours. A promise he makes in a chat (“I’ll check at five”) is kept in that chat.

#### Friends’ pings

A friend’s `@Edward` is someone else’s text driving a turn on your Mac, so it gets less:

- **No shell, file editor, Chrome or screens**, and `look` only at what they sent or a link. Those act as you on your machine. `EDWARD_FRIENDS_FULL_TOOLSET=on` gives friends everything, at the risk that a message (or a page it points him at) drives a shell running as you.
- **No new conversations**: anything he sends goes into that chat, or one that addressed him in the last 24 hours. He never writes to someone who asked him nothing, and leaves no task or reminder behind.
- **Limits**: six turns an hour per chat, more than three friends’ pings in five minutes stops him there (and tells you), and friends’ turns spend Edward’s own share of the daily cap, never your reserve.
- **Unknown numbers are held** for you, with a note at most once a day per sender, unless the chat is a group with someone from your contacts in it.
- **Your standing instructions come along**: if you told him to stay out of a chat, he stands down there and tells you.

What a friend’s ping can still do is read what Edward reads (your chats, memories and calendar) and answer from it. His prompt asks for discretion, but a prompt is not a wall: think about who can reach him before you turn Messages on.

#### Switches

- `EDWARD_PINGS=off` stops the runner; pings are still recorded, and the mind answers mentions instead. To stop answering altogether, turn Messages off in Listening.
- `EDWARD_PING_FRIEND_TURNS_PER_HOUR` (6), `EDWARD_PING_CONCURRENCY` (2), and the iMessage skill, which gates reading and sending.
- `GET /api/health/report` counts how every ping ended, by who asked, and how fast he answered.

### Photos, PDFs, voice messages and video

Attachments in a chat are understood, not skipped:

- Photos (HEIC, stickers, GIF frames) are converted with macOS’s `sips` and seen as pictures; a ping turn gets up to six images and one PDF inline.
- PDFs are read whole (up to 15 MB and 100 pages).
- Voice messages and videos are heard through ElevenLabs’ Scribe (once voice is set up) and seen through a small Swift helper built by `setup.sh` (frames from a video).
- Links are read first, from public addresses only, and never a sign-in or confirmation link, or one from an unknown number.

Images leave saved history as a line with their reference, so old conversations stay small. `EDWARD_MEDIA=off` brings back plain placeholders.

### Other ways in

- **Twilio** gives Edward a number of his own for SMS and WhatsApp. Webhooks are refused without a valid Twilio signature, and only your own numbers get an answer; anyone else’s text is held, unanswered.
- **The WhatsApp bridge** (whatsapp-mcp) reads and sends WhatsApp as you, once you run and pair it.
- **Alexa** can ask Edward through a custom skill, but inbound requests are not signature-verified yet: see [Guard rails](https://meet-edward.com/docs/guard-rails).

Want Edward on an Apple ID of his own, so people text him rather than you? That is a project; [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting) has a prompt for it.

The long form: [heartbeat.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/heartbeat.md), [pings.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/pings.md) and [media.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/media.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening

---

## His computer

*A shell, an editor and a browser of his own, on your Mac, with rails.*

### One toolset, everywhere

Edward has the same fourteen tools in every turn: your chat, voice, pings, his wakes, the screens’ pulse and scheduled events. What a turn may do with them is its **policy** (did you ask? may it reach people? may it push?), checked when a tool is called; a refused call comes back as an honest `Tool error:` with the reason.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bash` | A persistent shell in his home folder, sandboxed |
| `str_replace_based_edit_tool` | View, create and edit files, under the same rails |
| `web_search`, `web_fetch` | Search the web and read pages |
| `browser` | His own invisible browser |
| `chrome` | Your Chrome, through the Edward extension (off by default) |
| `look` | See images, PDFs, a web page or the screen as pictures |
| `messages` | Read iMessage and mail |
| `send_message` | The one guarded way to message someone |
| `tell_owner` | Reach you: a note on Today, or a push |
| `memory` | Search, remember, close, explain or forget memories; read and write documents |
| `schedule` | Reminders, follow-up wakes, your calendar and Reminders |
| `screen` | His screen, the household screen and the iPhone widget |
| `plan` | A visible checklist for longer work |

Skill switches only take tools away: Shell/Bash gates the shell and editor, Web Search the web tools, iMessage the message tools, iOS Widget the widget, Push Notifications the urgent push.

### His home and his shell

`~/edward-home` is his: `bin/` (on his PATH), `projects/`, `skills/`, `downloads/`, `jobs/` for background logs, and a Python 3.12 environment of his own. He may `pip install`, use `uv` and `npm`, and `brew install` ordinary formulae.

- One persistent `bash` per conversation, so `cd` and variables carry over between commands.
- 180 seconds a command; long work is a background job plus a scheduled wake to check on it.
- A watchdog kills a session past 2 GB of memory or when the disk runs low; at most four sessions at once.
- Every output is scanned and secrets are redacted before the model sees it.
- Its environment is an allowlist: no API keys, no `.env` values, no database address.
- If the sandbox can’t apply, `bash` fails closed. It never silently runs unsandboxed.

### The rails

The shell runs under a macOS Seatbelt profile rendered from one table of rails, which the in-process editor checks too:

- **Not his own credentials**: the session-signing key, the setup code and `.env`, however the path is spelled (compared by the file’s identity on disk, so case variants, symlinks and hard links count).
- **Not his own running code**: no writes to the checkout Edward runs from, his releases or his own sandbox config, and none of the directories above them can be renamed or moved.
- **Not what production runs on**: no writes to either Postgres cluster’s data or to Homebrew’s `python@3.12` and `postgresql@16`, and no upgrading them.
- **Not the services that act as you**: no connection to Edward’s own API (:8000, :3000), the WhatsApp bridge, or his databases (:5432, :5433).
- **Not your other apps**: no launching or scripting apps (messages go through `send_message`, never `tell application "Messages"`), never a second Google Chrome, and signals only to his own processes.

> **The sandbox is not a containment boundary.** The shell runs as your macOS user. Reads are open (except his own credentials), and writes are open everywhere but the protected paths, including your shell startup files, `~/Library/LaunchAgents` and Homebrew, from which programs later run as you, outside the sandbox. The rails stop accidents and turn misuse into deliberate work; they don’t make it impossible. For real isolation, run Edward under his own macOS user (prompt G in [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting)). Short of that, keep friends’ pings on their default, which gives them no shell.

### Two browsers

#### `browser`: his own

Playwright’s bundled headless shell, never Google Chrome, with his own cookies (never yours). It opens http and https only, and every request and redirect is checked: nothing on this Mac or your network, only public addresses. He can open, read, find, click, type, scroll and download.

#### `chrome`: yours, if you allow it

With `EDWARD_CHROME_HANDS=on` and the unpacked extension in `chrome-extension/` loaded, Edward can use your own, signed-in Chrome. The extension connects only directly from this Mac, and only Edward’s own extension ID is accepted. Rails:

- Typing outside a search box, pressing Enter there, or clicking anything labelled send, post, delete, accept, confirm, share and the like acts as you, so it runs only when you asked in that turn.
- A payment step, or typing anything that looks like a card number, is refused in every turn.
- Taking a picture of a tab never switches your active tab.

Chrome shows its “being debugged” bar while he works, unless you set `EDWARD_CHROME_SILENT_DEBUGGER=on`. With the hands on, `/screen` also opens as a tab in your Chrome (see [Widget, screen & hub](https://meet-edward.com/docs/surfaces)).

### `look`

`look` hands the model the picture itself, not another model’s description of it: a photo from a chat, a file, a PDF, a web address, his own page, your Chrome tab, or this Mac’s screen (which needs Screen Recording for the backend’s python). Images are scaled to 1600 pixels at most, never up; a turn carries at most 40 images.

### The web

On Claude, `web_search` and `web_fetch` are Anthropic’s server tools: the search and fetch run at Anthropic. With `EDWARD_SERVER_WEB_TOOLS=off` (or on the Codex fallback) they run locally: Brave Search with your key, and a local fetch that refuses this Mac and your network on every hop.

### Your calendar and Reminders

- **Reading**: straight from Calendar’s and Reminders’ own databases on this Mac (Full Disk Access), read-only, in every turn. If they can’t be read he says so; he never reports an empty day instead. apple-mcp, if set up, is the calendar’s fallback.
- **Changing**: only when you ask, through a small signed EventKit helper (macOS 14+). Grant it once, at the Mac, with `bash backend/scripts/eventkit_request_access.sh`. Edward never asks macOS himself, because a dialog nobody answers would hang a turn.

The long form, including the full list of what the sandbox does not prevent, is [computer.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/computer.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/computer

---

## Widget, screen & hub

*Where Edward shows himself, and decides for himself what to show.*

### The pulse

Edward decides what his surfaces show, the way you would decide what to pin to a fridge: there is no fixed layout. Every 15 minutes a check in code looks at what feeds them (the pet board, your calendar, the widget, the screens, who is at the hub). Only when something changed does he take a turn to decide what to show; most ticks cost nothing. The pulse reaches nobody and never pushes. If it fails or the day’s budget is spent, a plain fallback card stands in.

### The iPhone widget

A home-screen widget through the [Scriptable](https://scriptable.app) app. Edward fills it with sections (a title, lines, stats, a countdown) or, when he wants full control, a small Scriptable script of his own. A section can carry an end time and disappears by itself when it passes. Until he writes anything, the widget shows your upcoming events in your time zone.

#### Setting it up

1. Turn on the **iOS Widget** skill (Edward tab → Mind → Skills).
2. Install Scriptable and copy [`scriptable/edward-widget.js`](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/scriptable/edward-widget.js) into a new script.
3. Fill in your public address and your widget token: while signed in, open `/api/widget/token` on your Edward.
4. Add a Scriptable widget to your home screen and pick the script.

> **Treat the widget token like your password.** Besides the widget, it can chat with Edward as you (`POST /api/widget/chat`, which `scriptable/edward-chat.js` uses). Put it only on your own devices; if it leaks, replace it with `POST /api/widget/token/regenerate` while signed in.

### His screen

`/screen` is Edward’s stage, meant for a display near the host Mac (or any browser you like). It is a scene of up to eight pieces he places himself (words, notes, lists, a countdown or timer, a picture, a video, your calendar, the pet board, a clock), with Edward standing in it, the lines he says, and, while a wake or the pulse is running, what he is thinking: tool names and scrubbed reasoning, never their arguments or results.

![Edward's screen: a headline, a countdown to a landing, the weather for Saturday, a thought he wrote, tonight's pet care, and Edward standing on the stage](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/screen-desktop.png)
*A scene he arranged on a quiet evening.*

- **It is his.** He is encouraged to change it, and his free time each afternoon is partly for it.
- **Your ask holds it.** Ask him to put something up and it stays until the hold lapses; his own turns can’t replace it, though he can still say a line.
- **His lines** can be spoken aloud, never during quiet hours.
- **Opening it**: open `/screen` yourself in any browser. With the Chrome hands on, Edward finds or opens it as a tab in your Chrome, sized to the desktop (never a full-screen Space).

### The household hub (optional)

`/hub` is a touchscreen page for a kitchen or a pet station: a thin client, with all the logic on the host Mac. The reference install ran it on a Raspberry Pi with a 7″ touchscreen in Chromium’s kiosk mode ([pi-hub-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/pi-hub-setup.md)); any kiosk-mode browser on `/hub` works.

![The household hub: the time, two late doses, a who-toggle, Edward's greeting, tiles for pets, calendar, lists, voice, timers, health, photos and settings, and each pet's feeding status](https://meet-edward.com/screenshots/hub-kiosk.png)
*The hub on a 7″ kiosk: two doses late, everything else calm.*

| Page | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/hub` | Home: the day at a glance, and what Edward put up for the house |
| `/hub/pets` | Feeding and medication: tap to log a dose |
| `/hub/today`, `/hub/lists`, `/hub/timers` | The family calendar, shared lists, kitchen timers |
| `/hub/ask` | Full-screen voice. It runs as someone in your home, not as you |
| `/hub/health`, `/hub/settings`, `/hub/idle` | Vitals, the panel’s own controls, the photo screensaver |

#### Built so alerts stay rare

- Food given “twice daily, whenever” **never** goes overdue. Only timed doses (a dog’s 06:00 and 18:00 medication) can.
- A dose more than four hours late stops alerting, but is still recorded.
- Status colours never change with a person’s theme: “overdue” looks the same whoever is at the screen.
