- An item copied from, say, a pet-sitter’s note shows a “needs review” badge until someone confirms it.
- A timed dose still unlogged 45 minutes after its slot pushes you once per pet and slot, from code, outside quiet hours and the spend cap, unless someone is standing at the hub.

#### Setting it up

- **Pets and care** come from a seed file: copy `backend/hub_seed.example.json` (a fictional dog and a cat), describe your own, and set `EDWARD_HUB_SEED`.
- **People**: `EDWARD_HOUSEHOLD`, comma-separated, you first. With two or more, the hub shows a who-toggle and themes by person.
- **Photos** for the screensaver live in `~/edward-photos` on the host Mac; upload them from the Edward tab (House → Hub Photos). A photos-only second login for someone else in the house (`/photos`) is off unless `PHOTO_DOOR_PASSWORD_HASH` is set.
- **Over plain HTTP on your network**, the kiosk browser needs `--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure=http://my-mac.local:3000`, or the microphone, the wake lock and the sign-in cookie silently fail.

The hub signs in with your normal password, so it deliberately has no controls that change Edward himself (no restart button, no skill switches).

The long form: [screen-and-browser.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/screen-and-browser.md) and [hub.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/hub.md). For the pulse’s place among his wakes, see [The mind](https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/surfaces

---

## Guard rails

*One process reads untrusted text and can act as you. Here is what stands in between, and where it stops.*

### Before a password exists

- Until you choose a password, the API answers nothing but the sign-in pages.
- The first password needs a **one-time setup code** the backend writes to `backend/.setup_code`, readable only by your macOS user and deleted once the password is set. The request must also come from a page at `localhost` on the host Mac, but a device on your network can forge those headers: the code is what keeps someone else from claiming your Edward first.
- Wrong codes are limited (10 per client in 15 minutes); sign-in allows 5 failed tries per client in 15 minutes, and 100 across all clients.
- Sessions last 30 days and renew past half their life. The cookie is `Secure`: serve Edward over HTTPS.

### Money

- **A daily spend cap** ($5 over your local day by default). Background work stops first (at 60 %), then Edward’s own turns (at the cap); your own turns may run a $3 reserve past it. When the cap is reached he says so in a sentence, not an error.
- **Per-turn caps**: $3 for a turn you asked for, $1 for anything else, and 60 tool rounds at most.
- Every model call is priced and logged, and shown in the app.

### What leaves

- **The egress secret scan** is always on. Every message and file he sends, every shell command, every push, every URL he fetches or looks at, every search, everything typed in a browser and every argument to a custom MCP tool is scanned for keys, tokens, JWTs and private keys. A hit is refused, with only the kind logged. The exception is Anthropic’s server-side search and fetch (the default on Claude): their queries are checked only after the fact, and logged.
- **Redaction on the way in**: shell output, files he views and every local tool’s result pass through the same scanner before the model sees them (the server-side search and fetch results can’t be).
- **One send.** `send_message` is the only way he messages anyone: one recipient, a 10-minute dedupe, and a **recipient rule**. He may write to someone only if you asked, it is the chat the turn was asked in, they addressed him in the last 24 hours, or it is a live conversation; anyone else is your call. The app says “Sent” only when the message was delivered.
- **Your Chrome** (if you turned the hands on): typing outside a search box or clicking send, post, delete and the like needs you to have asked in that turn; payments are refused in every turn.

### Taint and approvals

A turn is marked tainted when it starts from untrusted content (a message, a mail, a wake’s pack) or reads some (a web page, your messages, a calendar invitation). The approval gate that can hold such a turn’s outward calls is **off by default**; the recipient and Chrome rules above do its job in code. Set `EDWARD_TAINT_APPROVALS=shadow` to log what it would have held, or `on` to hold each one for your Approve / Deny on Today. An approval runs the stored call once, and never past the secret scan.

### His computer

His shell runs under a macOS Seatbelt sandbox: it can’t read his own credentials (the session key, the setup code, `.env`), write the code he runs from or what production depends on, reach his own API or databases, or launch and script other apps. Details in [His computer](https://meet-edward.com/docs/computer).

> **It is not a containment boundary.** The shell runs as your macOS user and can write your shell startup files, your LaunchAgents and Homebrew, from which programs later run as you, outside the sandbox. A prompt injection that reaches the shell (a web page, a message, a file he was pointed at) therefore has a way to run code as you. The rails make that deliberate work rather than one mistaken command. For strong isolation, run Edward as a separate macOS user (prompt G in [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting)).

### Other people

- **Friends’ pings stay off your machine**: no shell, editor, Chrome or screens unless `EDWARD_FRIENDS_FULL_TOOLSET=on`. They can still read what Edward reads (your chats, memories, calendar) and answer from it; his prompt asks for discretion, which is a prompt, not a wall. See [Listening & pings](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening).
- **Twilio** webhooks are refused without a valid Twilio signature, and then only your own numbers get a turn. Anyone else’s text is held, unanswered, with no push.
- **The household hub’s voice** runs as someone in your home, not as you: it follows the recipient rule and never texts you.
- **A wake never messages you with `send_message`**; it reaches you only through `tell_owner`. And a wake can’t change or delete what you said.

### Known gaps

- **Alexa**: inbound requests are not signature-verified. Only the skill id is checked, and an Alexa turn runs as you, so anyone who learns the id and your URL can run a turn as you. Leave `ALEXA_SKILL_ID` unset unless you use the skill (the route then answers 503). [Adapting to your Mac](https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting) has a prompt (E) that adds Amazon’s verification.
- **The widget token is owner-equivalent**: it can chat as you. Keep it on your own devices and regenerate it if it leaks.
- **Postgres trusts local connections** (Homebrew’s default), so any program running as you outside the sandbox can reach it. The shell itself is refused.
- **Custom MCP servers’** environment values are stored in plain text.

### Emergency switches

`EDWARD_EGRESS_SECRET_SCAN=off` and `EDWARD_COMPUTER_SANDBOX=off` exist for emergencies only; the second runs his shell unsandboxed and logs every command. To stop Edward reaching anyone: turn Messages off in Listening, unset `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, and turn the iMessage and Push Notifications skills off.

The long form: [trust-boundary.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/trust-boundary.md), [auth-and-pwa.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/auth-and-pwa.md) and [computer.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/computer.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/guard-rails

---

## Skills & integrations

*The switches, and everything Edward can connect to.*

### Skills

Skills are switches in the Edward tab, under **Mind → Skills**. Every one starts off on a fresh install. Edward’s tools are the same fourteen on every surface, and a skill can only take some away; each row shows a live status that says what is actually true (“not paired”, “credentials rejected”).

| Skill | What turning it on gives him |
| --- | --- |
| **Shell/Bash** | His computer: `bash` and the file editor, in his sandbox |
| **Web Search** | `web_search` and `web_fetch` |
| **iMessage** | `messages` and `send_message`: reading and sending iMessages, and mail with them. Pings need it too |
| **Push Notifications** | An urgent `tell_owner` may buzz your phone; with it off, he leaves a note on Today instead |
| **iOS Widget** | The `screen` tool’s widget actions |
| **Voice Conversations** | Voice memos and live voice (with an ElevenLabs key) |
| **Code Interpreter**, **JavaScript**, **SQL Database** | Retired: “Edward runs this in his own shell now.” They gate nothing |
| Twilio SMS and WhatsApp, WhatsApp (MCP), Contacts, Apple Services, HTML Hosting, Alexa, Orchestrator, Claude Code Session | Status rows. Each reports whether its integration works; the switch doesn’t change Edward’s tools |

`memory`, `schedule`, `screen`, `look`, `plan`, `tell_owner`, `browser` and `chrome` are always present (`chrome` answers that the hands are off until you turn them on).

### Messages and mail

- **iMessage**: read from Messages’ own database, sent through AppleScript from your own Apple ID, signed as Edward. See [Listening & pings](https://meet-edward.com/docs/listening).
- **Mail.app** (iCloud or any account in it): read from Mail’s index on the Mac.
- **Gmail**: through Google’s API with an OAuth client of your own ([gmail-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/gmail-setup.md)). Email he sends goes out from your Gmail through the same guarded `send_message`, and never to you.
- **Twilio**: SMS and WhatsApp from a number of Edward’s own. Signed webhooks only, answering only your numbers unless `EDWARD_TWILIO_ANSWER_ANYONE=on`.
- **WhatsApp as you**, through the whatsapp-mcp project’s Go bridge: run it yourself, scan its QR code, then `MCP_WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true`.

Reading is open in every turn; what someone else wrote marks the turn as tainted (see [Guard rails](https://meet-edward.com/docs/guard-rails)).

### Your Mac’s own data

- **Calendar and Reminders**: read from their own databases (Full Disk Access); changed only when you ask, through the EventKit helper.
- **Contacts**: read from the AddressBook databases; Contacts.app only as a fallback.
- **apple-mcp** (optional, `MCP_APPLE_ENABLED=true`): only a fallback for reading your calendar when Calendar’s own database can’t be read; its other tools are not given to Edward. Install bun and clone apple-mcp (its location is `MCP_APPLE_DIR`, default `~/apple-mcp`).

### Search

On Claude, search and fetch are Anthropic’s server tools and need no other key. **Brave Search** (`BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`) is used only when they are off (`EDWARD_SERVER_WEB_TOOLS=off`) or on the Codex fallback.

### Your home

- **Alexa**: a custom skill can ask Edward things ([alexa-setup.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/alexa-setup.md)). Inbound requests are not signature-verified yet, so leave `ALEXA_SKILL_ID` unset unless you use it.
- **Home Assistant**: announcements on Echo devices (`HOME_ASSISTANT_URL`, `HOME_ASSISTANT_TOKEN`).
- **Presence**: the menu-bar companion, or any script with your widget token, tells Edward which Mac you are at.

### Custom MCP servers

MCP servers already installed (by a March install, for example) run with `npx` or `uvx`, and their tools are bound beside the fourteen, prefixed with the server’s name. You can switch, restart or remove them in **Mind → Servers**; this release has no way to add a new one from the app, and Edward can’t install servers himself any more (he runs `npx` in his own shell when he wants one for himself). Because nothing can tell what a custom tool does, every one is treated as outward: its arguments are secret-scanned, its results taint the turn and are redacted, a wake that uses one writes a journal entry, and it is refused in friends’ pings and in turns that may reach nobody.

A server runs as you, unsandboxed, with an allowlisted environment (no keys of Edward’s). Its own `env_vars` are stored in plain text in the database and its backups: don’t put a write-capable token there without meaning to.

### Also available

- **Hosted pages**: `HTML_HOSTING_URL` and `HTML_HOSTING_API_KEY` point at a small upload service that speaks its API. There is no default host, and Edward’s tools for it were retired.
- **The knowledge graph** (Graphiti and Kuzu), off by default: see [Memory](https://meet-edward.com/docs/memory).

### Removed

The Python, JavaScript and SQL sandboxes, Lightpanda, LangSmith, Find My and USPS tracking are gone. See [Upgrading from March](https://meet-edward.com/docs/upgrading) for the full list.

The long form: [integrations.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/integrations.md).

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/skills

---

## Adapting to your Mac

*Edward ran for months for one person in one home. Here is how to fit him to yours.*

Most of what was specific to that home is now a setting. A few places still assume the first host, and each is marked in the code with an `ADAPT:` note. The full list, with file and line, is [docs/ADAPTING.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/ADAPTING.md).

### Settings, not code

| What | Where it is read | Settings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who you are | `backend/services/owner.py` | `EDWARD_OWNER_NAME`, `_FULL_NAME`, `_ALIASES`, `_HANDLES`, `_EMAILS`, `EDWARD_HOUSEHOLD` |
| Where Edward runs | `backend/services/host_config.py` | `EDWARD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `EDWARD_LAUNCHD_PREFIX`, `EDWARD_TUNNEL_LABEL`, `EDWARD_BACKUP_DIR`, and more |
| What the shell scripts see | `scripts/lib/edward-env.sh` | The environment, then `.env`, then the default |

See [Configuration](https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration) for the settings themselves.

### Finding the seams

```
grep -rn "ADAPT:" --include='*.py' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.sh' \
  --include='*.swift' --include='*.js' \
  backend frontend scripts companion chrome-extension scriptable | grep -v node_modules
```

Each note has the same three parts:

```
# ADAPT: <what is specific to the original host, in one line>
#   How it works here: <what the code assumes>
#   To adapt: <the setting to change, or what to build>
```

The ones you are most likely to meet:

- **iMessage as you.** Edward sends and reads as the Apple ID Messages on the Mac is signed into, so “from me” means you. An Apple ID of his own means reworking the echo checks.
- **Mail.app’s index** lives under `~/Library/Mail/V10`, which changes between macOS releases (`EDWARD_MAIL_ENVELOPE_INDEX`).
- **Calendar’s and Reminders’ stores** are private Apple databases, checked on one macOS version; when they can’t be read he says so (the calendar falls back to apple-mcp when it is set up).
- **The protected Homebrew kegs** (python@3.12 and postgresql@16) and `HOMEBREW_PREFIX`, which the sandbox rails name.
- **The screen** is a Google Chrome tab sized over AppleScript when the hands are on; any browser works when they are off.
- **The hub** is laid out for one 7″ kiosk, and its pets come from a seed file with no editor in the app.
- **Alexa** inbound is not signature-verified.
- **Ports**: :8000 and :3000 are also written into the Chrome extension and the shell’s denied ports, so moving one means changing those too.

### macOS permissions

Almost every grant goes to the **backend’s python**: the real path of the python3.12 behind `backend/.venv`, which `setup.sh` and the LaunchAgent installer print. To grant it: System Settings → Privacy & Security → the list → **+** → `Cmd + Shift + G` → paste the path. Started by hand from a terminal, macOS charges the terminal app instead.

| Permission | What needs it |
| --- | --- |
| Full Disk Access | iMessage, contact names, Mail’s index, the Calendar and Reminders stores, and backups to a removable drive |
| Automation | Sending an iMessage; with the Chrome hands on, Chrome, Finder and System Events. Answer the first prompt at the Mac |
| Accessibility | Sizing Chrome’s window for `/screen` (hands on only) |
| Screen Recording | `look` at the screen |
| Calendars, Reminders | Changing them when you ask: `bash backend/scripts/eventkit_request_access.sh`, at the Mac |

> **Grants follow the binary’s path.** `brew upgrade python@3.12` moves Python and every grant silently stops applying: grant the new path, re-run `bash scripts/install-launchagents.sh` and the EventKit script. A `brew install` of something that depends on Python can upgrade it along the way, which is why Edward’s media handling avoids ffmpeg.

### Prompts for the bigger changes

Open Claude Code in your checkout: `CLAUDE.md` loads by itself and carries the house rules (a fix lands with the test that pins it, backend tests only on the test database, the architecture doc of anything you change). [ADAPTING.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/ADAPTING.md) has a prompt for each of these, ready to paste:

|  | Change |
| --- | --- |
| A | A pets-and-care editor in the Edward tab, so the hub needs no seed file |
| B | Linux, starting with a sandbox for the `bash` tool (bubblewrap) |
| C | systemd units instead of LaunchAgents |
| D | A separate Apple ID (or number) for Edward, so people text him, not you |
| E | Amazon’s signature verification for inbound Alexa requests |
| F | Your own browser (Safari, Arc) for the screen |
| G | Edward under his own macOS user, for real isolation of his shell. The reference install never ran this way: treat it as a project (his own logged-in session, his own copies of your data, Postgres with passwords) |

When you add code that assumes something about your own host, mark it the same way, and add a row to ADAPTING.md.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/adapting

---

## Architecture

*How Edward is built, run and tested.*

### Overview

```
Next.js PWA (:3000)  ──/api──▶  FastAPI (:8000)  ──▶  PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector (:5432)
Today · Chat · Voice                  │
Edward tab · /screen · /hub           │
                                      ├─ a turn (LangGraph): preprocess → retrieve_memory → respond (tool loop) → extract_memory
                                      ├─ one toolset of 14 tools; bash runs in a Seatbelt sandbox in ~/edward-home
                                      ├─ listeners: iMessage (chat.db), Mail, Gmail → the mind (wakes, noticing, pings)
                                      ├─ scheduler (every 30 s), consolidation (hourly), the screens' pulse
                                      └─ the Claude API: ChatClaude, one route per purpose, a daily dollar cap
```

The backend runs natively on macOS, never in a container: it reads Apple’s databases, talks to Messages over AppleScript, and sandboxes Edward’s shell with Seatbelt. The frontend is a Next.js production build served on :3000, which forwards `/api` to the backend. All state is in PostgreSQL: conversations and their LangGraph checkpoints, memories, documents, events, ledgers and settings.

### A turn

```
preprocess → retrieve_memory → respond (the tool loop) → extract_memory
```

- **One tool loop** for every surface (chat, voice, pings, wakes, the pulse, scheduled events), with the same [fourteen tools](https://meet-edward.com/docs/computer). What a turn may do is its `TurnPolicy`: whether you asked, whether it may reach people or push, where it may reply, its dollar cap and deadline. A turn you are not part of, with no policy, is fail-closed.
- **Honest failures**: every tool failure reaches the model as `Tool error: <the real error>`; the same failing call is refused the third time; after three failed rounds he is told to step back, and after six the turn stops.
- **Bounds**: 60 rounds, $3 a turn you asked for and $1 otherwise, 300 s per model call, 600 s per streamed turn, tool results capped at 30K characters.
- **One turn at a time in a thread**, and Stop cancels the step in flight. The turn’s trace (reasoning, tools, memory hits) is stored with the answer, so the work rail renders the same from history.

### The model

Every model call goes through one set of builders and one Claude adapter on the `anthropic` SDK, with a model, effort and prompt-cache lifetime per purpose (chat, mind, pulse, background, voice, judge). Before each request the adapter asks the daily spend cap, and after it prices the call into a ledger. Every call is labelled with what it was for (`mind:nightly`, `ping:friend`, `turn:chat`…), which is how the app shows where the money went. An unofficial Codex fallback exists behind `EDWARD_LLM_PROVIDER=codex`. Details in [Configuration](https://meet-edward.com/docs/configuration).

### Running in the background

| Loop | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduler | Polls every 30 s; each due event runs as its own task, in your time zone, never the host’s. Reminders, follow-up wakes, the nightly and free-time ticks, a five-minute sweep, the pulse. |
| Listeners | iMessage every 10 s, Mail and Gmail on their own intervals; they store events and nothing else |
| Ping runner | Answers each `@Edward` in its own turn, two at a time, never two in one chat |
| The mind | Wakes, the noticer and the speak gate ([The mind](https://meet-edward.com/docs/mind)) |
| The pulse | Every 15 minutes, a model turn only when a surface’s inputs changed |
| Consolidation | Hourly memory upkeep ([Memory](https://meet-edward.com/docs/memory)) |
| The sweep | Every five minutes, with no model: the late-dose alert, noticing upkeep, snoozes |
| Graph worker | Optional, its own LaunchAgent: fills the knowledge graph |

### Startup order

`main.py`’s lifespan starts things in an order that matters: the tool registry must come after skills and every MCP source.

1. Logging, the database and the LangGraph checkpointer (tables, migrations, drops)
2. The time zone cache, the embedding model, the Codex rate gate (Codex only)
3. The storage directory and skills
4. Built-in MCP clients (after an orphan sweep), custom MCP servers, a second skills sweep
5. The tool registry
6. Edward’s computer: his home, the Seatbelt profile, a sweep of leftover shells
7. The scheduler
8. The listeners and the mind path, the presence probe
9. The ping runner
10. Browser hands (a no-op unless they are on)
11. Consolidation (after 60 s)
12. The orchestrator (recovers crashed worker tasks; dormant)
13. Greeting pre-warm

Shutdown runs the matching hooks in reverse, his computer first.

### The chat stream

`POST /api/chat` streams Server-Sent Events, `data: {json}`, plus a heartbeat comment every 10 s when idle. Every event has a `type` and a `conversation_id`; the frontend folds them into one live bubble. A crash mid-stream becomes a spoken-style apology and `done`; a client that leaves gets nothing more, and the step in flight is cancelled.

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `user_message` | A voice memo’s transcript and audio, before the answer |
| `progress` | Steps such as memory_search, tool_execution, generating |
| `memory_match` | One per retrieved memory (debug streaming only) |
| `thinking` | The model is working between tool calls |
| `reasoning` | Summarized reasoning, as it streams |
| `tool_args_delta` | Partial JSON of a tool call being written |
| `tool_start / tool_end` | A tool call begins / finishes (result ≤ 500 chars) |
| `code, execution_output, execution_result` | A command, its output, its result |
| `plan_created, plan_updated, plan_step_update, plan_completed` | His visible plan |
| `cc_session_start, cc_text, cc_tool_use, cc_tool_result, cc_session_end` | A Codex session (dormant) |
| `content` | Text of the answer |
| `done` | Stream complete: the checkpoint is written, the thread is free |

### The tree

```
meet-edward/
├── backend/            FastAPI: main.py, routers/, services/, tests/, scripts/
│   └── services/
│       ├── graph/      the turn: the tool loop, streaming, the prompt
│       ├── toolset/    the 14 tools and TurnPolicy
│       ├── computer/   his home, shell, editor and the Seatbelt rails
│       ├── heartbeat/  the listeners and the mind path
│       ├── pings/      the @Edward runner
│       ├── media/      photos, PDFs, voice messages, video
│       ├── voice/      live voice
│       └── …           memory, mind, noticing, reach, scheduler, hub, screen
├── frontend/           the Next.js PWA (app/, components/, lib/, __tests__/)
├── chrome-extension/   his hands in your Chrome (optional)
├── companion/          the menu-bar companion
├── scriptable/         the iPhone widget
├── scripts/            LaunchAgents, the watchdog, the test cluster
├── docs/               ADAPTING, UPGRADING, architecture/
├── site/               meet-edward.com
├── setup.sh
└── restart.sh
```

### Running it

- **LaunchAgents** keep the backend and frontend alive, and run a health check every five minutes (Postgres, backend, frontend, the tunnel, the graph worker and the scheduler, bottom up, never restarting the app onto a dead dependency), a deeper one at 08:00, a verified nightly backup and a daily memory report.
- **The frontend is a production build.** `frontend/deploy-build.sh` builds the next version beside the running one and swaps it in on restart; `frontend/rollback-build.sh` swaps back. Open tabs reload onto a new build only when you are idle.
- **The live checkout is production**: edits there are live at the next restart, so build and experiment in a git worktree.

### Testing

- Backend tests run only on their own Postgres cluster on :5433, through `scripts/with-test-db-lock.sh`, never with the live database exported. They can never reach a real model, Chrome, Messages, your calendar or the embedding model.
- Frontend tests are `node --test`, with guardrail tests that pin real contracts (every tool has a work-rail label, one clock format, every settings panel in a room).
- A UX fixture harness runs the real app against a mock API with invented content, for screenshots and design work.
- Evaluation gates run the real model over recorded situations, with every outward act a dry run, before the mind, pings or noticing change.
- A doc lint fails when the docs name a path, route or event that doesn’t exist.

### Read further

- [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): the operating guide, every rule that must hold, every route and setting. Written for Claude sessions working in the repo, and just as useful for people.
- [docs/architecture/](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/tree/main/docs/architecture): one page per subsystem, with the reasons and incidents behind each rule.
- [api.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/docs/architecture/api.md): every route and socket.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ben4mn/meet-edward/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup for contributors, the checks a change must pass, and the privacy rules.

Source: https://meet-edward.com/docs/architecture
